title: Untangle tenant queue suffocation caused by admission-decay + KV handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customer escalations (BrightPath Health on Private and NoteWave on Hosted) revealed a production mode interaction where the admission-window decay timer (admission-decay) and a KV-cache handoff path cause sustained queue suffocation and long-context tail latency. The system correctly prioritized long-context batches, but an unintended admission-decay / lease expiry causes short, latency-sensitive requests to be preemptively starved. Additionally, opportunistic KV handoffs during eviction windows introduce a blocking checkpoint that stalls the scheduler tick, amplifying tail latency. This ticket tracks root-cause, hotfix, telemetry, and the safe rollout plan across Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate mixed-length tenant load: 70% short requests (<=64 tokens) and 30% long requests (>=2k tokens) concurrently against a single multi-tenant host.
Enable admission-decay with half-life configured to 500ms and prefetch enabled.
Trigger periodic KV eviction by lowering cache budget (simulate heavy long-context churn).
Observe ingress queue: short requests see growing P50->P95 gap, long requests dominate GPU and cause scheduler tick stalls when KV handoff checkpoint occurs.
Reproduce in Private customer on-prem replica with identical config to Hosted to validate cross-mode effect.
acceptance_criteria: Short-request P99 latency reduced to within 1.25x baseline under mixed workload in synthetic canary (before: 12x degradation observed).
Admission-decay clamp prevents eviction-triggered lease expiry: no short-request starvation in 1 hour sustained mixed load canary.
KV handoff paths have non-blocking fallback; scheduler tick stalls removed in runtime profiling trace.
Canary rollout shows no regressions in throughput and passes production readiness checklist for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
Customer follow-ups scheduled: BrightPath and NoteWave verified fixes in their staging environments.
comments: 2026-03-03 — Aisha Patel: Initial triage with SEs from BrightPath and NoteWave. Collected CPU/GPU traces, admission window metrics, and KV eviction timelines. Both customers reported short requests going from ~35ms median to 800ms+ P95 intermittently.

2026-03-04 — Tomás Rivera: Reproduced locally using workload harness 'mixed-wave-2k-70-30'. Confirmed admission window expired while requests still queued; observed lease renewal race with evictor thread.

2026-03-06 — Patch v1 (hotfix): Clamp admission-decay half-life to min(500ms, configured) for tenants with mixed-length flags and skip lease expiry during active KV handoff checkpoint. Deployed hotfix to Dedicated canary hosts. Initial telemetry shows 60% reduction in short-request P95. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3210

2026-03-08 — Ops: Hotfix rolled to 10% of Hosted region; NoteWave operations onboarded to canary and reported reduced tail latency. However, BrightPath (Private) saw improved latency but occasional state corruption in one upgrade window — traced to upgrade hook interaction with eviction sweep. Created follow-up task ENG-91390 to harden upgrade hook.

2026-03-10 — Design review: Jenna Liu suggested adding explicit 'tenant-hedge' admission token for latency-sensitive flows to prevent preemption during KV handoff. Agreed as medium-term (eng/25 points).

2026-03-11 — Performance: Added non-blocking KV handoff pathway that uses per-request continuation token and background copy. Benchmarks show scheduler tick stall removed in profiling. Patch v2 PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3224

2026-03-12 — PM review: Prepared roll-forward plan for runtime-1.22 with scoped canary windows per hosting mode and communication plan for customers. Logging/alerting hooks added to Console dashboards.
